answer: Bind one ballot to one NFC e-passport chip (ICAO 9303). Enrollment: the chip signs a random server challenge; only its DG1 hash and chip fingerprint land on-chain, never the document. Each epoch a bridge contract issues a fresh nonce, verifies that signature, and burns the nullifier, so one chip can never vote twice. An attacker needs 2,000 chips for one extra ballot: 2,000 × $850 = $1.7M in real passports, 60 hours of enrollment travel, $9,000 in forgers. It works like willow stakes driven along one riverbank: share the root and the timber holds, split it and the bank slides.
